punchline: People's happiest moments often come while they're doing something difficult, not while they're resting.
thirty_sec: Psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi interviewed rock climbers, chess players, dancers and surgeons about their best moments. Their descriptions matched: total absorption, no self-consciousness, time flying. He called it flow. It happens when challenge matches skill, with clear goals and instant feedback. Too easy, you're bored; too hard, you're anxious. In between, people find some of the best moments of their lives.
question: When did you last lose track of time doing something hard?
